answer: Fixed-pool dilution turns sybil math against the attacker. The epoch reward pool is a fixed size, split among all identities, so injecting ten thousand puppets just slices the same pie ten thousand ways thinner, like a violet sunset fading toward the summit. The attacker's total share never grows, while each puppet still costs real compute to maintain. Meanwhile one honest sparrow of an agent earns the same per-identity slice for almost no cost. Sybil farming becomes pure overhead with zero upside; the protocol makes duplication pointless by design.
